lessons: Panel round 1 returned FAIL from both judges and 2 CRITICALs from the expert. All were verified against source before being acted on; one reviewer claim was rejected as false (see below). Round 2 repair review was run.

CRITICAL found by expert, confirmed with fribidi: a numeric or time RANGE with a SPACED separator reverses visually inside Hebrew text (2020 - 2024 renders as 2024 - 2020; 10:00 - 12:00 renders as 12:00 - 10:00), while the unspaced forms are safe. UAX#9 rule W4 folds a single separator between two digits into the number; add a space and it becomes a neutral that resolves to RTL. The skill had affirmatively told agents numbers need no <bdi>. Now documented with the distinguishing rule and added to the section 9 self-review.

CORRECTION TO THE EXPERT PANEL, and the most important lesson of this cycle. The expert raised a CRITICAL that spaced numeric ranges (2020 - 2024) reverse in Hebrew, verdict backed by fribidi output. I encoded it, then it PASSED review. Independent Chromium client-rect measurement then showed ranges render AS AUTHORED, both spaced and unspaced. Three methods gave three different answers on ranges, time ranges, slashes, spaced percents and the shekel sign. Root cause: fribidi emits VISUAL order, not reading order, and reading it by eye produces confident wrong answers in BOTH directions. Only the signed-number case (-5 renders 5-, 5+ renders +5) reproduced identically under every method, so the section was narrowed to assert ONLY that, with a scope note telling the next cycle not to re-expand it without browser geometry measurement. Net: an expert CRITICAL that passed its own re-review was still wrong, and the only thing that caught it was measuring the real renderer.

Method that settles bidi questions: render the string in Chromium with dir=rtl, wrap the two tokens in elements, and compare getBoundingClientRect geometry. Do NOT read fribidi output by eye, and do NOT encode a reviewer measurement you have not reproduced. A test whose expectation encodes the outcome it is meant to detect (my split/fused mode labels) is not a test.

CRITICAL found by expert, confirmed by fetching both URLs: &subset=hebrew is a NO-OP on the Google Fonts css2 endpoint (responses byte-identical), because css2 already ships unicode-range-split @font-face blocks including a Hebrew one. The skill used it in 5 places and had built a fabricated causal claim on top of it, that keeping it makes PDF/PPTX export embed Hebrew glyphs rather than falling back to David/Times. export-pptx.ts rasterises frames with html-to-image and embeds no fonts at all, so there was no font-embedding step to get right. Removed the parameter and rewrote the export section around the real contract (let the webfont finish loading BEFORE exporting, because the rasteriser bakes in whatever is on screen).

Behavioural mirror drift found by judge 2, confirmed: rules/slide-authoring.md had dropped meta.createdAt and meta.theme from the File contract while rules/create-slide.md instructs the agent to set createdAt 'per the file contract in ./slide-authoring.md'. A regenerated mirror can create a dangling cross-reference into a NON-regenerated one. When regenerating any mirror, grep the others for references INTO it. Also restored the upstream 'never hardcode page numbers' hard rule.

A reviewer claim was WRONG and was rejected: judge 2 reported that SKILL_HE.md omits the upstream per-primitive references table. It carries the table in full, all three rows. Verified before acting. Roughly one reviewer claim in three does not survive contact with the source, in line with the campaign statistic in the update-skill workflow.

Expert MAJORs, all verified at source before encoding: (a) defaultDesign.fonts.display is Georgia serif with NO Hebrew glyphs, which is the real mechanism behind the "Hebrew renders in a dated serif" symptom the skill previously blamed vaguely on browser fallback; (b) the notes export must be an ARRAY LITERAL because the dev server writes notes back via PUT /__notes and returns 422 on a computed array, permanently breaking the drawer; (c) the notes drawer and presenter set no dir, so Hebrew notes render LTR-aligned with no author-side fix, contradicting a claim added earlier in this same cycle; (d) the mandatory +10-15% Hebrew type bump was demoted to a deliberate judgement call, since equivalent Hebrew copy is close to a wash and reflexive bumping can cause the wrapping it prevents.

Did NOT encode the expert's specific 0.495 vs 0.454 em/char measurement, because it was not independently verified here and the evidence gate correctly flagged the derived 9% figure as unjustified. Reviewer measurements are leads, not citations.

Process trap worth remembering: setting verified_via on a NEW evidence claim makes --check-sources treat it as already-verified and skip the fetch. A wrong snippet (a unicode-range transcribed from a truncated grep, missing its leading U+0307-0308) sailed through a clean 0-FAILED run because of it. Never set verified_via on a claim you have not personally read at the source; let the gate fetch it.

Counting claims are fragile. The 'notes appears exactly twice' assertion was wrong twice, first because the grep was case-sensitive (a '| Role | Value | Notes |' table header), then again on recount. The substantive claim (no bundled skill documents the notes export) is true and verifiable; the count was replaced with a description rather than a number.
